concepts.name: Meaning of Demand
concepts.description: Demand refers to the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to purchase at different prices during a given period. Demand requires both willingness to buy and purchasing power.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define demand and distinguish it from desire or want.

concepts.name: Determinants of Demand
concepts.description: Demand is influenced by factors such as the price of the commodity, consumer income, prices of related goods, tastes and preferences, population, and future expectations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and explain the major determinants of demand.

concepts.name: Individual and Market Demand
concepts.description: Individual demand refers to the quantity demanded by a single consumer, while market demand is the total demand of all consumers in the market.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to differentiate between individual demand and market demand.

concepts.name: Law of Demand
concepts.description: The law of demand states that, other things remaining constant, the quantity demanded of a commodity decreases when its price increases and increases when its price decreases.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the law of demand with suitable examples.

concepts.name: Demand Schedule and Demand Curve
concepts.description: A demand schedule presents the relationship between price and quantity demanded in tabular form, while a demand curve represents the same relationship graphically.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to construct and interpret a demand schedule and demand curve.

concepts.name: Assumptions of the Law of Demand
concepts.description: The law of demand assumes that factors such as consumer income, tastes, prices of related goods, and population remain unchanged.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to state the assumptions underlying the law of demand.

concepts.name: Extension and Contraction of Demand
concepts.description: Changes in quantity demanded caused solely by changes in the commodity's own price result in movement along the demand curve.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between extension and contraction of demand.

concepts.name: Increase and Decrease in Demand
concepts.description: Changes in demand due to factors other than price cause the entire demand curve to shift either to the right or to the left.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain shifts in the demand curve using practical examples.

concepts.name: Demand Curve Movements
concepts.description: Students study the difference between movements along a demand curve and shifts of the demand curve caused by non-price factors.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to interpret movements and shifts in a demand curve.

concepts.name: Price Elasticity of Demand
concepts.description: Price elasticity of demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to changes in the price of a commodity.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the concept of price elasticity of demand.

concepts.name: Degrees of Elasticity
concepts.description: Demand may be perfectly elastic, perfectly inelastic, relatively elastic, relatively inelastic, or unitary elastic depending on consumer responsiveness.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify different degrees of price elasticity of demand.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Elasticity
concepts.description: Elasticity depends on factors such as the availability of substitutes, nature of the commodity, proportion of income spent, and time available for adjustment.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the factors influencing price elasticity of demand.

concepts.name: Consumer Decision Making
concepts.description: Understanding demand helps consumers make rational purchasing decisions based on price and income changes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply demand concepts to everyday consumer decisions.

concepts.name: Business Pricing Decisions
concepts.description: Producers use demand analysis to determine pricing strategies, estimate sales, and maximize revenue.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how businesses use demand analysis in pricing decisions.

concepts.name: Government Policy
concepts.description: Governments analyze demand while designing taxation, subsidies, and public welfare policies to influence market outcomes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to relate demand analysis to government economic policies.

concepts.name: Understanding Demand
concepts.description: This chapter explains the meaning of demand, determinants, the law of demand, demand schedules and curves, changes in demand, elasticity of demand, and their practical applications.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze demand, interpret demand curves, explain elasticity, and apply demand concepts to real-world economic situations.
